claim: A large replication (N=399) found no unconscious thought advantage; Bayes factor 7.83 favoured the null.
quote: the large-scale replication study yielded no evidence for the UTA
authors: Nieuwenstein, Wierenga, Morey, Wicherts, Blom, Wagenmakers, van Rijn
title: On making the right choice: A meta-analysis and large-scale replication attempt of the unconscious thought advantage
transfer: none. Warns against a 'diversion step' (leave the problem and return) as a decision aid; test any such step against a no-break arm.

claim: The meta-analysis of 61 effect sizes shrank from g=0.15 to g=0.018 after trim-and-fill, so earlier positive effects were small-sample and likely biased.
quote: there exists no reliable support for the claim that a momentary diversion of thought leads to better decision making
authors: Nieuwenstein, Wierenga, Morey, Wicherts, Blom, Wagenmakers, van Rijn
title: On making the right choice: A meta-analysis and large-scale replication attempt of the unconscious thought advantage
transfer: none. Do not add an 'incubate then decide' stage for choice tasks without measuring it.

claim: Unconscious thought did not beat immediate decision or conscious thought in deception detection; Bayes factors favoured the null.
quote: unconscious thought was found to be no better than immediate decision and conscious thought
title: Do Not Think Carefully? Re-examining the Effect of Unconscious Thought on Deception Detection
transfer: none. A second null: delay-then-decide does not generalise to judgment tasks.

claim: Sio and Ormerod's meta-analysis of 117 studies gave only a low-to-medium incubation effect, d about 0.29.
quote: the overall average effect size was in the low-medium band (mean d = 0.29)
title: Incubation and Intuition in Creative Problem Solving
transfer: Incubation is a modest gain: a cheap optional 'step away and return' call for open divergent tasks, not a core step.

claim: Incubation benefit was larger after an undemanding interpolated task than a demanding one, but another study found no effect of break demand or length.
quote: no effects for length of break or for the demandingness of the activity during the break
title: Incubation and Intuition in Creative Problem Solving
transfer: Mixed boundary condition. If testing a break step, vary what fills it and measure; do not assume.

claim: Evidence argues against the idea that people secretly keep working on the problem during the break.
quote: it seems safe to rule out the Intermittent Work explanation of incubation effects
title: Incubation and Intuition in Creative Problem Solving
transfer: Descriptive. Leaves the unconscious-processing explanation open, which gives no program step.

claim: The unconscious-work account fits small, knowledge-rich tasks such as divergent thinking, and is untested for knowledge-lean insight problems.
quote: is most applicable to relatively small scale but knowledge rich problems such as divergent thinking tasks
title: Incubation and Intuition in Creative Problem Solving
transfer: Use incubation-like steps only on open knowledge-rich tasks (idea lists), not on puzzles. Matches our own puzzle losses.

claim: Thoughts about the target during a break did not predict later performance quality (Baird et al. 2012, as reviewed).
quote: frequency of target task related intermittent thoughts during incubation was not related to quality of performance
title: Incubation and Intuition in Creative Problem Solving
transfer: none. Cannot judge incubation quality from how often the model revisits the problem.

claim: Most 'insight' problems were solved by ordinary analytic processing; only about 8% of insight-reported solutions involved an impasse.
quote: The results indicate a typical, analytic solution method consistent with the business-as-usual theory.
title: Insight problem solving is not that special, but business is not quite 'as usual': typical versus exceptional problem-solving strategies
transfer: Do not build the agent around waiting for an impasse and a flash. Default to analytic search; treat restructuring as an escalation.

claim: Convergent thinking, inductive reasoning and analogy predicted insight-problem success; divergent thinking explained only about 2% of variance.
quote: Divergent thinking explained only about 2% of the variance.
title: Insight problem solving is not that special, but business is not quite 'as usual': typical versus exceptional problem-solving strategies
transfer: On insight-style puzzles, spend calls on convergent checking and analogy retrieval, not forced divergence. Fits our ARC and word-puzzle losses.

claim: Verbal non-insight problems were hurt 29% by articulatory suppression and 24% by tapping, so dual-task cost is not unique to insight.
quote: solving verbal NIPs seems to be equally vulnerable when performed concurrently with either a verbal or a motor task
title: Insight problem solving is not that special, but business is not quite 'as usual': typical versus exceptional problem-solving strategies
transfer: none. Descriptive.

claim: The review proposes the default network generates candidate ideas from memory and the control network evaluates them, but the evidence is functional connectivity, which is correlational and not ubiquitous.
quote: Default-control network coupling is not ubiquitous.
title: Creative Cognition and Brain Network Dynamics
transfer: Procedure: generate candidates from memory with loose control, then a separate evaluate-and-revise call against the goal. Evidence for the split is correlational; test it, do not assume it.

claim: In poetry, default-control anticorrelation during generation weakened during evaluation, so the generate/evaluate split is not clean in time.
quote: possibly due to increased task demands and top-down control required
title: Creative Cognition and Brain Network Dynamics
transfer: Allow evaluation to interleave with generation instead of strict phases; compare strict vs interleaved on a held-out set.

claim: The memory account of idea generation is largely speculative: episodic retrieval occurred infrequently in one task.
quote: retrieval of episodic memories during performance of this task occurred infrequently
title: Creative Cognition and Brain Network Dynamics
transfer: none. Do not hard-wire a retrieve-memory-then-recombine step on this evidence alone.

claim: The cited studies used small specialised samples (poets, pianists, art students) and mixed analysis methods, limiting transfer.
quote: The studies cited involve professional poets, professional pianists, and art students.
title: Creative Cognition and Brain Network Dynamics
transfer: none. Limits transfer from experts to general reasoning.

claim: Control-network subnetworks differ: one correlates positively and one negatively with the default network at rest, so 'the control network' is not one thing.
quote: FPCNa positively correlated with the default network and FPCNb negatively correlated with the default network.
title: Functional realignment of frontoparietal subnetworks during divergent creative thinking
transfer: Descriptive. Suggests splitting evaluate into separate checks (goal fit, feasibility, novelty) rather than one critic.

claim: Only one control subnetwork's coupling with the default network tracked individual creative ability.
quote: the strength of FPCNb-default network connectivity correlated with individual creative ability
title: Functional realignment of frontoparietal subnetworks during divergent creative thinking
transfer: Weak. Brain-network links to ability give no prompt-level procedure.

claim: The neuroimaging literature on creativity and insight is described as self-contradicting, with no single critical region (72 studies reviewed by Dietrich and Kanso).
quote: creative thinking does not appear to critically depend on any single mental process or brain region
authors: Dietrich and Kanso (as quoted in a Frontiers review)
title: A review of EEG, ERP and neuroimaging studies of creativity and insight (second-hand, via Frontiers in Human Neuroscience 2014 review)
transfer: none. Reason not to copy any single neural signature into the agent.

claim: Kounios and Beeman report an EEG alpha change in right visual cortex before insight; I found no replication or critique in my searches, and the NSF story says closing one's eyes can produce it.
quote: About one and a half seconds before the subject pressed the button, the EEG in the right visual cortex began to oscillate at a very low frequency.
title: What happens when aha strikes
transfer: Preparation-state idea: cut inputs before a restructure attempt (shorter context, drop failed attempts). Untested for models; try as an ablation.

claim: Deliberate mind wandering predicted creative performance but spontaneous mind wandering predicted lower performance, from trait questionnaires.
quote: deliberate MW positively predicted creative performance, whereas spontaneous MW was negatively associated with such performance
title: Mind wandering and creativity (trait study)
transfer: Directed loosening beats undirected drift. Use a deliberate 'explore unrelated ideas' call with a stated aim, not random noise.

claim: People favour feasible, typical ideas when selecting; originality correlates negatively with feasibility.
quote: originality correlates negatively with feasibility
authors: Nijstad et al. (as summarised in a secondary review)
title: The Shifting Sands of Creative Thinking: Connections to Dual Process Theory
transfer: A model critic will likewise prune odd ideas. Score novelty separately and keep top-novelty ideas through evaluation; check with distinct-answer counts.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction by LLMs without external feedback can lower accuracy on reasoning tasks.
quote: their performance even degrades after self-correction
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: The evaluate step must use an outside signal (test, run, new inputs) or abstain from revising. Never reflect and revise on opinion alone.
